utterances.text: -- after they burnt house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let me just go through that then a little bit more slowly. I know you explained in your statement that the women and children were in the courtyard and that as you've just explained that Sali Rexha's house had been set on fire. Can you explain to us who set the house on fire and how that was done?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: The force, the very forces that separated men from women.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did you observe how the house was set on fire, this house?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you explain to the Court what you saw, how that was done?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: When they separated women and children, they sent them there, but first they set fire to it with those inflammable things they had. And then they sent the women and children there to see the terror that was taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Are you able to explain -- you've explained that they had these inflammable things or devices. Can you explain what you saw and how it was exactly, if you saw this, how they set that house on fire?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain it to you. It was a kind of round thing, a cartridge, I think. It was like a bottle, in the shape of a bottle, and with that thing they set the houses on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you some questions now about what happened with the men. I know you described briefly for us today and also in your statement the Serb forces dividing the men. Are you able to explain to us in a bit more detail how the men were divided by the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes. They divided them in three groups. The first group was taken to the house of Sali Rexha Gashi, the second group to the house of Sadik Gashi, the third to the house of Deme Gashi. After they took them inside, you could hear the rifle shots; and immediately after that, they set the house on fire to do away with any trace.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And I'll -- I'll follow that up again with you, sir, in some detail. Before we do that, can you tell us how far apart these houses were from one another?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: The house of Sadik from Deme's house are about 30 metres from Deme's, from Azem's house are about 70 metres apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And I notice that in your statement you sometimes refer to the house of Azem Gashi and other times you refer to the house of Azem Rexha. Can you tell us, are those the same people, or is that the same person?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes. Azem Rexha Gashi has father's names -- name and his last name. That's why I refer to him by that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that's clear. Can you tell us as well which house did Syl Gashi normally live? I know at times you've referred to his house. Was that the same house as one of those three?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Syl Gashi is the son of Azem Rexha Gashi, but we called him Muharrem. In the papers his name was recorded as Syl.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So would it be correct, then, that the house of Syl Gashi is the same as the house of Azem Gashi?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let me take you through now, if I can, what happened to these men with each house. If we can deal first -- you describe in your statement in paragraph 56 the first shootings being heard in Azem Gashi's house. Can you explain to us what you saw and heard with respect to that house?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: When they took the first group there, I heard automatic rifle shots and then saw the flames after five minutes to burn the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And you say that you saw flames. Did you see how that fire was started?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Not at Azem's house, because it was impossible to see who set the fire; but after five minutes, I could see the flames and the smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You describe the next firings that you saw and heard being in Sadik Gashi's house. Can you explain what you saw and heard there?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: The second group was taken to Sadik Gashi's house, and they did the same thing as the first case. They killed and burned them. And among them I saw Hazir with his broken leg trying to walk away from that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And the third set of shootings that you described in your statement was at Deme Gashi's house. Can you explain to the Court what you heard and saw there?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: They brought ten men to the house of Deme Gashi, took them inside the house, killed them with automatic rifles, and Rexhe Isuf Kelmendi managed to survive. He was in the room. It was his luck to survive the shooting. He escaped from the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And I'll have some questions for you as well about what you saw, what happened in the aftermath. Before I go there, just so that we're clear, can you explain again how far you were from these houses when you made these observations? Were you in the same place that you described previously?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I was 50 metres behind Deme's house. I was lying on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Are you able to describe the -- the forces, the people who were doing these acts, who were firing these shots and who were burning these houses?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: These people were dressed in police and army uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you describe for us what those uniforms looked like?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Blue and green camouflage, but the faces I couldn't see properly because it looked like horror movies, like the Ninjas.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And when you say like Ninjas, is that because of the bandannas? Am I understanding that right?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: From the face you could say that. All my life I have never seen such horror-stricken faces, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us who Qash Lushi was?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us who Qash Lushi was? Was he one of your fellow villagers?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: No. His name is Qaush Lushi, with "ch".

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Qaush Lushi, can you tell us who he was? Was he one of your fellow villagers?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes. That day when they divided men from women, in order to save his son from the massacre they asked him to pay them 100.000 euros, and he asked his wife to go and fetch the money. He gave the money, then the son was massacred, and Qaush was slit on his neck in front of the house where the first group was executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I think we may have had a problem just with the interpretation on the last part. You said something about his neck. Can you explain what happened after he gave the money?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: They slit his throat.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did you see that yourself or how you did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I saw it with my own eyes. They put him in the toilet, and they cut off his head with a Kalashnikov.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far approximately you were from that when you made that observation?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I was behind the house of Deme Gashi, and the distance from the site of the event was about 60 metres, because the toilet was located on the lower part in the same direction where I was lying.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: When you say toilet, is this the toilet in a house or is this an outhouse? Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: It was an outhouse in Azem Gashi's yard. It was Azem's toilet in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And again, just so we're entirely clear, can you explain who it was who was doing this, who it was who killed him?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: The same persons that were there in Qyshk's massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I do have some more questions for you about that, but I see that we're nearing, I think, the time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is so, Mr. Behar. We must have a break now, and we resume in half an hour. The court officer will assist you during the break. We will resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, when we left off, you had just finished telling us about this murder that had taken place, or this killing that had taken place in an out house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can I have up Exhibit 05258, please, on the screen. I'll need photo number 6. It's not coming up. 05258. Just a moment's indulgence, Your Honour. I think there's an issue with the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Just while that's being resolved, perhaps I'll try to come back to that. Perhaps we can have up P00772 from earlier in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, there's a photo of a man -- can you see the photo on your screen?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: There's one of the men depicted in that photo in the centre at the top or at the back. Can you tell us, do you know this man, sir? Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: The one in the middle? Yes. This is Salipur, and he was an active policeman in Peja.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us how it is that you know him?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I know him because on the 26th of March, Ram Xhemajli Kelmendi in Qyshk, he was 98 years old and he was killed by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Is that something you saw or did you hear about that from somebody?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Uk Kelmendi, Ram Xhemajli's son told me the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Had you had any dealings with Mr. Salipur in the past, and can you explain how you came to know who he was?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: He was a very dangerous person. He was a very serious and well-known criminal in the Balkans.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And had you seen him in your town or nearby?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I used to see him in Peja, because he was an active policeman in Peja for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And just in terms of timing, can you say when you would see him? Is this the same year? Is this the previous year?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Before the war in Kosova I used to see him several times. Not just once, several times. His name was Munja. He was a very dangerous person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Returning to -- to the events of May 14th that you were describing for us, you explain at paragraph 61 and 62 of your statement that Serb forces at this point, after these -- the shootings and the burnings of the three houses with the men in them, that after that took place, the Serb forces took the women and children out of Sali Rexha's yard, loaded them onto tractors and sent them to Peja. Can you tell us, sir, were your wife and children in that group of women and children?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did you see the convoy leave yourself? Did you see this group of people leave yourself?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes, on tractors.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us what direction they headed in?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: They were directed towards Albania in order to cover up what they had done and hide the bodies of the people that had -- they had killed in Qyshk. They directed the people towards Peja, and then they told them to go back up to Zastava and then they told them to go once again in the same direction three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And I know that what you're describing now you also described in paragraph 64 of your statement. Can you tell us how it is that -- that you know that, that you know where the convoy was going and when?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: My wife, my son, and two daughters were there where the tragedy happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, I -- I'd like to, if I can, now, sir, focus on the observations that you made of those houses where the men had been and what you saw after the Serb forces left. Can you tell us, sir, what it is that you saw, what observations you made of those houses and of your fellow villagers?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: In the beginning I was following what was going on when Avdi Berisha was killed right before my eyes. I returned to the place where I was earlier, and I tried to bring the bodies out so that they would not burn, because I knew that today would come, today that I would be able to tell the story. There was such a big fire that it was impossible to tell whether there had been bodies there or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So perhaps we can discuss your observations of the houses individually. Can you tell us what observations you made at this time, after the forces had left and you went to see the house, at the house of Azem Gashi. Can you describe what you saw there?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I found the bodies burning. Flames were coming out of them. I thought I would go crazy. I could see the bodies moving because they had not died yet. They had been burnt alive, even though they had been shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Were there any survivors from that house, the house of Azem Gashi?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Only Hazir Berisha in Sadik Gashi's house. Ninety-five per cent of the others had been charred. Even two hours later, when I went there, the bodies were still, some of them, moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I know you mentioned Mr. Berisha and Sadik Gashi's house. Can you explain what observations you made in that house at Sadik Gashi's house?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: The men were taken there. They were killed and then set on fire. Hazir Berisha is a survivor. He had been injured on his leg, and he tried and managed to climb out of the window and escaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did you observe that yourself? Did you see his escape?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did you see Mr. Berisha afterwards as well, after he had escaped the house?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: No. It was impossible, because he went into the wheat field. Behind the house of Sadik Berisha there was this wheat field, and that's where he went.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can we have up photo -- sorry, Exhibit P00797, please. And I need photograph number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Just a moment, sir. It's not this photo I'll ask you about, but another one. Sir, do you recognise the building that's being shown in this photo here, what's left of that building?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: This is Sadik Gashi's house, and the person here is Hazir Berisha from Qyshk, the one who survived the massacres -- the massacre when the Serb and Slav forces executed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Finally, I would ask you about any observations you made afterwards at the house of Deme Gashi. Are you able to explain what you saw in that house, in the aftermath of the shooting and the burning that you described?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: The same situation as in Sadik's house. Ten men were taken into the house. They were killed and then set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, in paragraph 57 of your statement you speak about the survivors of these massacres. I'll just read that to you. You say: "Later on I learnt that Isa Gashi survived execution in the house of Azem Rexha. Then Hazir Berisha survival or survived from the killing in the house of Sadik Gashi, and Rexhe Kelmendi survived execution in the house of Deme Gashi." I know you described seeing Mr. Berisha escape. Are you able to tell us how you knew that Isa Gashi and Rexhe Kelmendi survived?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Rexhe Isuf Kelmendi climbed out of the window, because when they were taken inside, the policeman ordered him to take the matches and set the house on fire, and then after that, he climbed out of the window and escaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you explain how it was that you learned what you just told us? Is that something you saw, or did someone tell you that?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Rexhe, when he came out of the window, I saw him. I was 50 metres away from the window and from the house, and I beckoned to Rexhe to come to where I was, because otherwise he would have been caught and killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And how about with Isa Gashi? Is that something that you saw yourself, or was that explained to you, or how did you learn about his survival?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I could not see Isa because Isa was 60 or 70 metres away from the place I was, but after we were trying to take the bodies away from the houses on fire, I met him and he told me what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So you've mentioned now taking the bodies away, and I wanted to ask you some questions about that as well. I know that in paragraph 70 of your statement you describe hiding the bodies of the people who had been killed. Can you explain to the Court why you felt that you needed to hide these bodies and who you were hiding them from?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: From the police, because they wanted -- they were interested to cover up everything. They wanted to burn them and -- so that nobody would know what had happened there, destroy the traces, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Are you able to explain to the Court how you hid those bodies?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes. When they were killed, and then burnt, myself, with the help of Mustaf Krizbuki [phoen] and some other villagers, we managed to pull the bodies away. It was impossible to bury them on the same day because there were civilians. 1.240 people were sheltered there. And I took plastic sheets, wrapped the bodies individually, and then we opened a big grave and buried them there all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You mentioned a little while ago in your testimony the name Avdi Berisha. Can you explain to us what happened to Avdi Berisha?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: When I was observing the police forces leaving Qyshk, because I knew that they would go to Pavlan because Qyshk and Pavlan are very close to each other, next to each other, Avdi's house was about 60 metres from the asphalt road, and he was killed by a -- by a sniper 3 metres away from me, right in front of my eyes. A police sniper killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And again just so we're clear, did you observe him being shot by the police?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could just have a brief indulgence. I just wanted to check on the status of that exhibit I was trying to show earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption. It's being worked on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I wanted to ask you as well. You described people on this day, on the 14th of May, being set out -- sent out, deported from the village of Cuska. I wanted to ask if you yourself had ever made any observations prior to these days, before this time, of any other Albanians who were travelling in a large group like that.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes. People in Peja suffered more than us in Qyshk.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And are you able to explain what it was that you saw, what observations you may have made of people from Peja?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I saw the convoys going towards Montenegro in order to escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you describe where you were when you made those observations?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: All the time I was moving around because I wanted to know what was going on and what was happening to the Albanian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So were you making these observations from Cuska, from your village, or where did you make them from?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: No, closer, because I could see the fire and the smoke. I had never before and never since seen in my life such fire and such smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So I'd like to focus on that a little bit then. Can you explain where you were seeing this fire and smoke?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I was a shepherd, I had cattle, and I saw everything that the Serbs did. What they did, what they burnt, how they forced the population out to go through the fields.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: But again just so we're clear, is what you're describing, was that in Peja that you saw that? I'm just trying to help the Court to understand where this was that you were seeing things.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I saw these things in Peja, and people also told me how they had been expelled. There was great confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us then, I know you mentioned a convoy earlier, are you able to explain what that looked like? And by that I mean approximately how many people you saw and how they were travelling.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: There was a large number of people. There were cars, tractors. It was an extraordinary number of people. From the town people were walking or going to some other place, and if people are in such great numbers, it's easy to see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did you see this on the road somewhere or where were the people walking?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Peja's exit towards Montenegro can be seen from the field because it's a flat area. You can see everything from the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And are you able to tell us when you made these observations?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date. However, this happened before the Qyshk massacre. As I said, the exact date escapes me. They expelled the people, and they burned the whole town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Would this have been in the same year as the Qyshk massacre you described? Can you give us a rough approximation? Was it months before, a year before?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes. In the same year. I think it was not even one month before, but as I said, I can't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And I just wanted to clarify an earlier answer. When I had asked you did you see the road or where was this road that you were describing, you described Peja's exit towards Montenegro. I just wanted to ask you again so we're clear. Can you explain where -- where this road was? Maybe -- maybe it's best to explain where it was in relation to Peja and to Cuska.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: The road Peja-Mitrovica, 3 kilometres out of Peja, there is this arrow that shows the direction towards Montenegro, and that's where I saw the people who were travelling, who were going in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And just one more clarification question about this area. When we're talking about Peja, are you referring to the town of Peja itself or to the larger municipality? Are you able to explain that?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: The town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. I do just briefly have two exhibits or two photographs I'd like to show you. If I could just have a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I wonder if it's possible to put these up on the ELMO. I can explain, Your Honours. These were part of the previous 65 ter number -- okay. It's up already. I see. These were part of the previous 65 ter number. I understand they were deleted when they were briefly put in. Actually, if I could have the other photograph first.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, you were discussing earlier in your testimony this killing that took place in the outhouse, and I'm wondering if you're able to identify this structure that we're seeing here.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I cannot see it. Ah, yes. This is the place where Qaush Lushi's head was cut off. This outhouse is about 15 metres away from the house. His head was cut off with an automatic rifle, and on these panels here, boards, you can see the bullet holes that cut -- of the bullets that cut his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And perhaps we could have the other photo up now as well, sir. I believe this is just a close-up of what you've just described. Are those the bullet holes that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the bullets that cut off his head, because he paid a hundred thousand euros and his son Astrit was killed, and then he himself was killed in this outhouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender those photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And they would be assigned P00804, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Those are my questions for you, sir. Thank you very much. And my learned friend on the Defence will have some questions for you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. If I may have a moment for preparation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kelmendi, good afternoon. My name is Dragoljub Djordjevic. I appear on behalf of the accused, Mr. Djordjevic. I have a few questions for you in order to clarify some of the facts that you were asked about by my learned friend, Mr. Prosecutor. Mr. Kelmendi, what is your profession or vocation?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I am a farmer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: What is your educational background?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Eight years of schooling.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: How did you get in touch with the Prosecutor's office of The Hague Tribunal, since I can see that you provided your first statement in 2008, on the 22nd of May.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I met them earlier as well, because eight members of my family were burned in the fire as Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: When was the first time that you provided any sort of statement by -- to this Tribunal? Is that the statement that was tendered dated the 22nd of May, 2008?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: No, it was earlier. When NATO forces entered and Kosova was liberated, I gave an interview at the site where the massacre happened. Euro News also reported on the massacre on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kelmendi, are you sure in 1999 when you say NATO entered Kosovo that you provided a statement to representatives of the International Tribunal, or was it to representatives of some other international organisation?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I gave statements to the people who were interested to know about the Qyshk massacre. I don't know why those statements are not reflected here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know which organisations those people represented to whom you gave a statement concerning the Cuska massacre?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I don't know. I was distressed at the time because of the things I had experienced and the things I had seen committed by the Serb forces. It was unimaginable what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that, but I would still like to ask you whether you remember that in 1999 you gave any kind of statement to any representatives of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Italian KFOR knows this better.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kelmendi. Am I right in saying that your village is actually in the outskirts of the town of Pec?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you describe where your house was exactly in relation to the road between Pec and Pristina from the direction of Pec?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: My house is 300 metres far from the asphalt road as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who Hazir and Fadil Berisha are?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes. They are my co-villagers from Qyshk village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: When you referred to the person leaving the house of Sadik Gashi that was on fire, was it one of the two people that we are discussing here now?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Hazir Berisha is the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: My question is this: The person you saw leaving the house of Sadik Gashi that was afire in May 1999, being the only person to survive the shooting in the house, do you know who that person was?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: This person is Hazir Berisha, the person who was one of those killed. He is a living testimony to the massacre when the forces acted against them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly? Are you saying that that person was killed?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Hazir escaped with a broken leg, and with his body in flames he managed to escape the massacre. I explained this even earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I understood you to be saying something else. I apologise. How far was the house of Hazir and Fadil Berisha from your house?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: It is interesting, but Hazir's house is in another street. Mine is in another street. But as the crow flies, we are about 300 metres away from each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be able to do something for me on a clean sheet of paper or perhaps with the assistance of some technical equipment that this Tribunal has, to -- would you be able to indicate where the Gashi house was as well as the house of Hazir and Fadil Berisha, and where were you exactly when you witnessed the events of the 14th of May, 1999? Would you be able to make a sketch, first of all Hazim Gashi house, Fadil Gashi house, and the place where you were at observing everything.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to assist the witness so that he would be able to use the electronic pen in order for him to be able to make a sketch as regards the house of Azem Gashi, then Sadik Gashi's house, as well as the house of Deme Gashi and to mark these houses with the letters A, S, and D respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it's going to be more practical with paper, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation] [In English] Obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Please put a square where the house of Azem Gashi should be, and put a letter A next to it. And the next square where Sadik Gashi's house should be and mark it with an S. And make a third square representing the house of Deme Gashi, and you mark it with a D. Also put another square or circle, mark it with an X, to reflect the position that you were at.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't a question, actually, although I will have a question afterwards. But on this piece of paper please put squares to indicate the houses of Azem, Sadik, and Deme Gashi, where the events took place. Mark the house of Azem Gashi with an A, the house of Sadik Gashi with an S, and the house of Deme Gashi with a D. Also put a circle and mark it with an X to mark the spot where you were. That is what I wanted to ask you.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Could you also please mark the place where the outhouse was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: One at a time. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: First of all, the house of Azem Gashi, put an A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The three houses are marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now you want to put an X with a circle to show the location where the witness was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And then one further thing. Beyond the X, what else did you want marked, the outhouse?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the outhouse where Qaush, I believe, was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's already marked. The witness is well ahead of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What about the position X? I don't see that? Where was the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: What are you indicating? Is that the place where you were?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I was here, behind the house. From here I could see that they gathered the people here, and then they took to Azem's house. I was lying here all the time. I saw everything from the beginning to the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please be able to mark with an X in a circle where you were near the house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: If I understand this correctly, you were behind Deme Gashi's house.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this drawing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned D00119, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: The next thing I would like to ask you is this: What is the distance between the place where you were and Deme Gashi's house, approximately?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: It is about 14, 15 metres. Of course I could -- I didn't measure it, but I tried to come as close as possible to the place of event. I saw Azem's son in the crowd, and I tried to go as close as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: How far is Deme Gashi's house from the house of Azem Gashi, in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: About 60 to 70 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: How far is Deme Gashi's house, in your opinion, from the house of Sadik Gashi?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Very close. They are separated by the main road that goes to Azem. Maybe 40, 50 metres, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: How far is Sadik Gashi's house from the house of Azem Gashi? In your opinion.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Maybe a little bit more, because Sadik's house is near the graveyard, on a lower place. I don't know what to say. They are very side by side. Neck to neck I would say, but I never measured it. I don't want to give you an exact figure because I am not a surveyor, a land surveyor, to measure it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In any case, that was not my intention. I wanted to hear your opinion about the distances. The outhouse, I see that the closest house to it was the house of Azem Gashi. How far is it from that house, in your view?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: The outhouse might be 10 metres away from Deme's house. So I would say 40, 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: The usher took away your drawing, but I saw a number there, a 10. Did you put that to indicate the distance between the outhouse and the house itself? I can see that on the drawing, and the paper is being brought to you.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Number 10 shows the distance between the outhouse. It was a public outhouse for the village. It was 10 metres far from Azem's house, outside the road, this outhouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The place behind Deme Gashi's house where you were, was there any growth there, tall grass? Is it a flat area, a depression? What does that location look like right behind Deme Gashi's house?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: It is a canal. There are growth -- green growths. It is a very dense foliage there. Only the birds can find you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Knowing the culture and way of life of Kosovar Albanians, I would like to ask you this: Around the houses of Azem, Sadik, and Deme Gashi, were there any brick walls or not?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: No, no. In Kosova there are no walls. After Communism was collapsed, we did away with all walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: When did that take place in your village that you tore down the walls?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: On the day that we handed over the membership cards, the party cards, we did away with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: You know that better than I.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't. That's why I'm asking you. When did Communism cease in Kosovo and Metohija? What year was that? I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I don't know the year. I don't know which year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Are you quite certain that even today there are no brick walls around any of Albanian houses?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: It is a fact that there are no brick walls. If you don't believe me, come with me. I have my Besa being an Albanian. You can come with me and see yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm merely posing questions here, and I have some information that points otherwise. The next question I have has to do with the photograph that was shown to you first by the Prosecutor. On that photograph you recognised one person by the name of Salipur, aka Munja. You also used some other adjectives concerning that person. My question regarding the photograph, I think it is Exhibit P00772 if I'm not mistaken, it is the group photograph use by my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have that brought back to the screen.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. [Interpretation] I will have a few questions for you regarding this photograph. This photograph that you're now looking at, is this the first time that you see it?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: No, sir. This is the last time I'm seeing this gentleman, because I have seen him alive. He has done everything possible short of eating people alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that this is not the first time that you see this photograph? You have seen this photograph before, the one that you're looking at now?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I saw him live in civilian clothes, in uniform, this person. Before -- even before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: You didn't understand my question. I'm asking you about the photograph, not the person nicknamed Munja whose last name was Salipur. I'm asking you about this photograph. Is this the first time that you see this photograph? That's what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: No. I have seen that many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: When did you see this photograph for the for the first time, Mr. Kelmendi?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: It's absurd to ask me such a question. This was a very bad person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: When was the first time that you saw this photograph, Mr. Kelmendi?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I said earlier when.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how much earlier than the events of the 14th of May, 1999? Approximately. Did you see it for the first time in recent times or immediately after KFOR was deployed in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I saw him for thousands of times. I told you. Do you understand me or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't, because I'm asking you about the photograph, not about Salipur. I'm asking you about the photograph. Let's imagine that Salipur is not there, although you do recognise the photograph. I'm asking you about the photograph. When did you see the photograph for the first time in relation to 1999? Was it immediately after the war stopped and after KFOR was deployed in Kosovo and Metohija or was it recently?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes, when the KFOR came, when they showed us the photos of the criminals, it was then that they I saw this photo for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: When you were shown photographs of criminals, did they tell you these are criminals, or did they ask you, "Are these criminals?" And please tell me right away who showed you the photographs.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: No. They asked me whether I knew the persons in the photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I believe that was the case. And can you tell me who asked you that and who showed you the photographs?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: The people who were authorised to inquire about the crimes committed in Kosova. Of course I can't remember their names. I can't tell you who they were, because I didn't have any power to ask them who they were, what they were doing. In our tradition, we don't ask too many questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me if they were Albanians or foreigners?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: They were foreigners.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question: Have you ever from any NGO or any other person received a book with this photograph and other photographs, including the one of your neighbour who survived the massacre, Hazir Berisha, as a gift?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I don't have any -- know anything about a book. I haven't seen any book. I don't know anything about a book.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Immediately after the events of the 14th of May -- or, rather, 1999, you say that together with some of your neighbours you moved the bodies away so that the Serbian police or the military or whatever couldn't come and remove the bodies. My question to you is this: After the 14th of May, did anyone from the Serbian forces come back to the village regardless of who it was, to look for the bodies of those who were killed in the houses of Azem, Sadik, and Deme Gashi? Did anyone come back after the 14th to look for the bodies and, if so, did anyone question the villagers about the circumstances and the whereabouts of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Yes. They came on the 16th. They came at Ymer Kadrija's house and asked about the men of the village. He said, I know nothing. They came again on the 17th to know who was killed, who had remained alive. When they found out that I was alive, they came three or four days afterwards at my door and fired a Kalashnikov, but I was lucky to escape. And after that, I tried to keep a very, very low profile to hide, because I no longer trusted anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, do you know who came on the 16th and the 17th of May and on that occasion when you were fired at? And when I say that, I'm not asking whether you knew the person, but I'm asking you also how many of them came. Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Four people came the first day. They usually came by car. On the 16th and 17th, they came in uniforms, police uniforms. One time they came in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what kind of a car they had, what kind of a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: It was a private car. They played two roles. When NATO had its strikes, they used private cars. When -- otherwise they used official cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Were those ordinary cars or jeeps, or something else, the official cars?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: The ones that came to the village you mean? Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: You said that during the NATO air-strikes they used -- they would come in ordinary private cars, and when there were no NATO air-strikes, they came in official cars. The official cars were those again just passenger cars with the army or military or whatever insignia, or were there -- were they some kind of special cars on the 16th, the 17th, and I don't know what May -- when you were fired and you -- at and you escaped.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: You are mixing up a question. When there were NATO air-strikes they used civilian cars. Otherwise, they used official ones. They came to the village after the massacre in civilian cars, black Mercedes cars they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you after the 14th of May see Ranko Vlahovic, Obrnovic, or Brajovic, any of the three? You yourself.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: After the war, I no longer saw them. It was impossible to see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Not after the war. Before the war ended but immediately after the 14th of May, let's say until the 11th of June. Did you see any of the three?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: After that day, I no longer saw anyone, because as I said, I kept away from the asphalt road because I was very much afraid. I wanted to remain alive, to be able to come here and to testify to what occurred that day in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kelmendi, let us go back to the photograph that is on our screens. I would like to ask you how did you immediate Salipur aka Munja who is depicted on this photograph? What were the circumstances, and could you tell me which person is he on this photograph out of all those people?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: This one near the flag in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So under what circumstances and when did you first see him?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: Before the war I saw him beating someone in front of my eyes in Peja.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what were the circumstances? Was there a war or was there no war? Did you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: No, there was not a war. It was before the war, but he -- he hated Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: And this person that he was beating, did you know that person?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: He beat him for nothing, for no reason at all, simply because he was Albanian. That person was reduced to such a state that we had to give him first aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what was the name of the person? You must have memorised that person's name since you went through this traumatic event. It's a major incident, and it was in peacetime. Was he in civilian clothes when he was beating that person or in a uniform?

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: This is really ridiculous what you are putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is actually quite sad, and I wouldn't agree with you that it's really ridiculous. If somebody is beating another person purely because the other person is Albanian, that's really sad. Well, if you want to answer my question, please do so, and then we'll continue tomorrow. This man Salipur Munja was he in a uniform or in civilian clothes when he was beating that person, and could you tell me what was the name of this person that he was beating for no reason, because as soon as you say that he was beating this person for no reason at all, it must mean that you are aware of all the circumstances surrounding this incident. That's why I'm asking you this.

utterances.speaker: TAHIR KELMENDI
utterances.text: I didn't know the person. This occurred 15 years ago, but the later massacre in Qyshk belittled the first incident that I mentioned. I apologise for using the word "ridiculous."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you, Your Honour. It is time for us to take our break, and I will -- I would like to continue my cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kelmendi, we must stop now because another trial will be conducted in this courtroom, so we must adjourn, and we'll ask you to come back tomorrow morning at 9.00 to continue. A court officer will give you further assistance when we adjourn. So we will see you again tomorrow morning, and we now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of May, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
